in_hebrew.name: עדגר
in_hebrew.meaning: מקור השם: השם הגרמני Edgar, סימן של חזון וכוח
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם: השם הגרמני Edgar, (אטמר, 'שדה', 'מגדל' + g(e)ard, 'שומר') - סימן של חזון וכוח. בספר 'דוד האב' של פטר אלט, Edgar (1264-1329) היה רוזן מאברסברג, וסייע לאלברט הראשון, דוכס אוסטריה, במסע הצלב השביעי. השם Edgar, שמקורו בגרמניה, היה נפוץ באנגליה בתקופה הנורמנית, והשם Edgardo (אדגרדו) היה השם האיטלקי/ספרדי לשם Edgar. Edgar (1295-1327) היה מלך סקוטלנד, ואחד מצ'יפסי הבולטים של העמק.

in_greek.name: Εντγκαρ
in_greek.meaning: Ονομασία: Γερμανική, από Εδγκάρ, σημαίνει 'στιγματισμός' και 'עוצמה'
in_greek.long_meaning: Ονομασία: Γερμανική, από Εδγκάρ, (Atamar, 'χώρα', 'κτίριο' + g(e)ard, 'φύλαξ') - σημαίνει 'στιγματισμός' και 'עוצμότητα'. Ο Έντγκαρ (1264-1329) ήταν κόμης του Αβέρσμπεργκ και βοήθησε τον Αλβέρτο Α' της Αυστρίας στη 第 Seventh Σταυροφορία. Ο όρος Έντγκαρ, που προέρχεται από τη Γερμανία, ήταν συνηθισμένος στην Αγγλία κατά την εποχή των Νορμανδών, και ο όρος Εντγκαρдо (Εδγαρδου) ήταν η ιταλική/ισπανική εκδοχή του όρου Έντγκαρ. Ο Έντγκαρ (1295-1327) ήταν βασιλιάς της Σκωτίας και ένα από τα φημισμένα 'τσεπ' της κοιλάδας.

in_latin.name: Edgardus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Germanicum, ab Atamar, 'terra' et 'aedificium', et g(e)ard, 'custos', derivatum est - significare 'speciem' et 'potentiam'. Edgardus, qui anno 1264-1329 vixit, comes Averbregensis et Albertus I, dux Austriae, in Sexta Crusade auxilii fuit. Nomen Edgardus, a Germania proveniens, in Anglia tempore Normannorum frequentissimum fuit, et Nomen Edgardo (Edgardu) Italiae et Hispaniae in usu fuit. Edgardus, qui anno 1295-1327 regnavit, rex Scotiae et unus ex 'chiefs' Vallis fuit.

in_english.name: Edgard
in_english.long_meaning: Edgard is a Germanic origin name, derived from the combination of Atamar, 'land' and 'building', and g(e)ard, 'guardian' or 'protector' - meaning 'vision' and 'power'. In the book 'David the Father' by Peter Althaus, Edgar (1264-1329) was the Count of Averberg, and assisted Albert I, Duke of Austria, in the Seventh Crusade. The name Edgar, originating from Germany, was common in England during the Norman period, and the Italian/Spanish name Edgardo (Edgardu) was the adaptation of the name Edgar. Edgar (1295-1327) was the King of Scotland, and one of the notable 'chiefs' of the valley.

data.cultural_impact: The name Edgard has deep cultural roots, originating from the Germanic language. It was a common name in Europe, particularly in Germany and England, during the Middle Ages. The name holds a sense of wealth, power, and protection, which would have been highly valued in these times. Many knights and nobles bore the name as a symbol of their position and strength.
data.spiritual_significance: Edgard is a name that embodies the concepts of wealth and protection, but it also carries a deeper spiritual significance. The name implies a strong sense of guardianship and protection, both in a physical and spiritual sense. It suggests a willingness to defend and uphold values, as well as a deep sense of responsibility and commitment. Moreover, the name may also be seen as a reminder of the ultimately protective nature of God, who watches over and guards us from harm. Overall, the name Edgard conveys a sense of strength, protection, and spiritual depth, making it a powerful and meaningful choice for a Christian name.
